verdict.rationale: SavvyCal documents a REST JSON API with OAuth and personal access token auth. Its endpoints cover bookings (list, create and cancel events), event types as scheduling links (update and duplicate), and reading available slots, so the core of building scheduling into a product is there. The evidence does not show availability itself being managed (writing schedules or hours) or links being created from scratch. Missing for 10: documented endpoints to create and delete scheduling links, endpoints to manage availability schedules rather than only read slots, a published OpenAPI spec (probes returned 404), and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, a documented REST API lets me manage event types, availability, and bookings programmatically — enough to build scheduling into my own product

citations.quote: The SavvyCal API adheres to REST conventions. Our API communicates in JSON format and uses OAuth access tokens to authenticate requests.
List events GET /v1/events ... Cancel event POST /v1/events/{event_id}/cancel ... Create event POST /v1/links/{link_id}/events
Update a scheduling link PATCH /v1/links/{link_id} ... Duplicate a scheduling link POST /v1/links/{link_id}/duplicate
